definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 defines object property as 'A name that may be used to qualify an object reference to get a value from or pass a value to an object' and property as 'property; object property: See object property'; §2023:3.137 reads 'name that can be used to qualify an object reference to get a value from or pass a value to an object'. Only 'may' became 'can'; the same names qualify the same object references, so the identifier-4 operands the exception admits are the same.

band-formats.answer: The 2002 band FORMAT 3 is the program-prototype format; 2023 merged 2002's Format 1 (on-overflow, archaic: §2002:14.8.4.1 'NOTE ON OVERFLOW is an archaic feature') and Format 2 (on-exception) into its Format 1, so the program-prototype format became Format 2. The two program-prototype diagrams are identical phrase for phrase (AS NESTED / program-prototype-name-1, BY REFERENCE identifier-2 | OMITTED, BY CONTENT and BY VALUE with arithmetic-expression-1, boolean-expression-1, identifier-4, literal-2, RETURNING, ON / NOT ON EXCEPTION), and neither band reaches the on-overflow or on-exception formats. No 2002 format is left unreached; no split.

behaviour-switch.answer: The two switches decide only whether a CALL of a restricted program-pointer AS program-prototype-name-1 requires the two prototypes' signatures to be the same (DialectBehavior.CallRestrictedPointerSignatureSame: §2014:14.9.4.2 SR14, no 2002 rule) and which CALL operands the ANY LENGTH screen covers (DialectBehavior.CallAnyLengthOperandRuleByFormat: §2002:14.8.4.2 SR10 in every format, split by format from 2014). This rule forbids omitting BY CONTENT for an identifier-4 permitted as a receiving operand, a spelling rule neither switch reads.
